text: In the Dexter et al. (2019) microfluidics study of the single-celled ciliate Stentor coeruleus, which observation was essential for showing the declining contraction response was genuine habituation (learning) rather than fatigue or receptor exhaustion?
choices: The cells stopped contracting permanently and never recovered
The contraction response grew stronger with each repetition
Habituation was stimulus-specific (cells habituated to fluid flow still responded to other stimuli) and recovered after a rest period, with dishabituation by a novel strong stimulus
The cells divided more rapidly after habituating
explanation: Genuine habituation is defined by stimulus specificity, reversibility with rest, and dishabituation by a novel strong stimulus, all of which Stentor met, ruling out fatigue or receptor saturation. Permanent loss of response (option 0) would instead suggest damage; a strengthening response (option 1) is sensitization, the opposite of habituation; and division rate (option 3) is irrelevant to the criteria.
